subtitle: How a Jain Monk Made a Kingdom Speak Forever

panels.shot: majestic low-angle wide of an elephant in a palace courtyard, a massive manuscript resting on a cushioned platform atop it, with Hemachandra standing calm beside the foreleg
panels.action: Hemachandra stands in serene profile beside a richly caparisoned elephant bearing a great bound manuscript on its back, with Patan’s sandstone temples and palace walls rising behind under a golden sky.

dialogue.text: In Solanki Gujarat, they said even an elephant once carried Hemachandra’s grammar like royal treasure. How did a Jain monk’s words climb so high?

i18n.hi: सोलंकी गुजरात में कहते हैं, एक हाथी ने भी हेमचंद्र की व्याकरण को राजखज़ाने की तरह ढोया था। एक जैन साधु के शब्द इतने ऊंचे कैसे चढ़े?

panels.shot: slow push-in from high balcony view over Patan, showing bustling markets, temples and the palace complex
panels.action: From a lofty vantage, the city of Patan stretches out: markets throng with traders, temple shikharas pierce the sky, and the royal palace dominates the centre as Hemachandra, in plain monastic robes, quietly observes the city below.

dialogue.text: Mid-twelfth century Patan: capital of the Solankis, crossroads of deserts and seas. Here, a Jain monk named Hemachandra would turn the speech of Gujarat into a kingdom’s memory.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी का पाटण: सोलंकियों की राजधानी, रेगिस्तानों और समुद्रों का चौराहा। यहीं जैन मुनि हेमचंद्र ने गुजरात की बोली को राज्य की याद बना दिया।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot inside a Jain monastery hall, shelves of palm-leaf manuscripts behind
panels.action: Inside a cool, pillared hall of a Jain monastery, rows of palm-leaf bundles rest on wooden shelves as young Hemachandra, shaved head and simple white robe, bends over a manuscript, stylus poised in deep concentration.

dialogue.text: Born in the traders’ world of Gujarat, trained in Jain learning, Hemachandra was shaped by libraries, not battlefields. For him, palm leaves were weapons, and syllables, soldiers.

i18n.hi: व्यापारी गुजरात में जन्म, जैन विद्या में दीक्षा — हेमचंद्र को रणभूमि नहीं, पुस्तकालयों ने गढ़ा। उनके लिए ताड़पत्र हथियार थे, और अक्षर, सिपाही।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot in the royal court, with the king implied off-frame and courtiers watching
panels.action: In the ornate Solanki court hall, Hemachandra stands composed with joined hands before an unseen ruler, while jeweled courtiers glance with a mix of curiosity and respect at the unadorned monk.

dialogue.text: Prabhachandra’s Prabhavakacharita recalls how Hemachandra entered the Solanki court, first under Jayasimha Siddharaja and then Kumarapala, his learning drawing kings into the orbit of a monk.

i18n.hi: प्रभावाचंद्र की ‘प्रभावकचरित’ बताती है कैसे हेमचंद्र पहले जयसिंह सिद्धराज, फिर कुमारपाल के सोलंकी दरबार में पहुंचे, और उनकी विद्या ने राजाओं को मुनि की कक्षा में खींच लिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up over Hemachandra’s shoulder, showing a palm-leaf manuscript with neat lines of script
panels.action: Over Hemachandra’s shoulder, we see his steady hand inscribing compact Devanagari-like characters on a narrow palm leaf, several tied bundles of earlier texts stacked methodically beside him in a lamplit study.

dialogue.text: He knew Sanskrit’s ancient grammars. Yet in Patan’s streets and courts, another tongue flowed. Hemachandra asked: can the living speech of this land be shaped with the same precision?

i18n.hi: वे प्राचीन संस्कृत व्याकरणों के उस्ताद थे। पर पाटण की गलियों और दरबारों में दूसरी ज़ुबान बहती थी। हेमचंद्र ने पूछा: क्या इस जीवित बोली को भी उतनी ही सटीकता से गढ़ा जा सकता है?

panels.shot: wide shot of a teaching scene, Hemachandra addressing a small group of disciples with tablets in hand
panels.action: Seated cross-legged on a raised platform, Hemachandra gestures gently as a circle of disciples sit below, each holding palm leaves, listening intently in the quiet of the monastery courtyard.

dialogue.speaker: hemachandra
dialogue.text: Rules must serve speech, not bind it to pride.

i18n.hi: नियम भाषा के काम आएं, घमंड की जंजीर न बनें।

dialogue.text: The Siddha-Hema-Shabdanushasana took shape here: a grammar that moved from Sanskrit through Prakrit to Apabhramsha, mapping three worlds of language on a single lattice of rules.

i18n.hi: यहीं ‘सिद्धहेम शब्दानुशासन’ तैयार हुआ: एक व्याकरण जो संस्कृत से प्राकृत होकर अपभ्रम्श तक चलता है, एक ही नियम-जाल में तीन भाषाजगत का नक्शा।

panels.shot: diagrammatic-feel wide shot: multiple language names inscribed on different manuscripts lying around Hemachandra
panels.action: In a symbolic arrangement, Hemachandra sits at the centre of a low writing table, surrounded by labeled bundles of manuscripts representing Sanskrit, Prakrit and Apabhramsha, his face lit by an oil lamp as if linking them all.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars note his boldness: he treated Apabhramsha, ancestor of Gujarati and Rajasthani, as worthy of system. Not a corrupt slang, but a language that deserved its own chapter.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान उनकी हिम्मत पर ध्यान दिलाते हैं: उन्होंने अपभ्रम्श को, जो गुजराती और राजस्थानी का पूर्वज है, व्यवस्था के काबिल माना — बिगड़ी बोली नहीं, अपना अलग अध्याय चाहने वाली भाषा।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Kumarapala (implied by a crowned figure) listening to Hemachandra in court
panels.action: In the court, a crowned king seated on a carved throne leans forward, listening as Hemachandra, still seated on the floor, explains with calm gestures, while ministers look on, weighing the monk’s words.

dialogue.text: Under Kumarapala, Hemachandra’s influence deepened. Prabhachandra paints a picture of a king who would consult the monk not only on doctrine, but on history, poetry and the conduct of rule.

i18n.hi: कुमारपाल के राज में हेमचंद्र का असर और गहरा गया। प्रभावाचंद्र एक ऐसे राजा की छवि खींचते हैं जो मुनि से केवल धर्म नहीं, इतिहास, कविता और राजकाज पर भी सलाह लेता था।

panels.shot: medium shot with split composition: Hemachandra dictating while scribes write on multiple manuscripts
panels.action: In a spacious scriptorium, Hemachandra dictates calmly while several scribes sit in rows, each copying on palm leaves that will become the Abhidhana-Chintamani, the Kavyanushasana and other works.

dialogue.text: Grammar was only one pillar. He built a dictionary, Abhidhana-Chintamani. A manual of poetics, Kavyanushasana. A Yoga-shastra. A vast Jain universal history: the Trishashti-shalaka-purusha-charita.

i18n.hi: व्याकरण केवल एक स्तंभ था। उन्होंने शब्दकोश ‘अभिधाना-चिंतामणि’ बनाया। काव्यशास्त्र ‘काव्यानुशासन’। एक योगशास्त्र। और विशाल जैन विश्व-इतिहास ‘त्रिषष्ठि-शलाका-पुरुष-चरित’।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of Hemachandra pointing to a painted scroll of kings and cities
panels.action: Hemachandra stands beside a long illustrated scroll showing kings, cities and battles, his finger tracing the line of Gujarat’s rulers as a royal audience watches the narrative unfold.

dialogue.text: In his Dvyashraya, he wove grammar into the story of the Chaulukyas. Language and dynasty shared a double foundation: the same book taught how to speak and how Gujarat had been ruled.

i18n.hi: ‘द्व्याश्रय’ में उन्होंने व्याकरण को चालुक्यों की कथा में पिरोया। भाषा और वंश, दोनों दो सहारों पर टिके; वही किताब सिखाती थी कैसे बोलना है, और कैसे गुजरात पर राज हुआ।

panels.shot: evocative wide shot of an elephant caparisoned in the palace courtyard, watched by courtiers and townspeople
panels.action: In the palace courtyard, a richly adorned elephant stands ready, a broad, canopied platform strapped to its back as courtiers, monks and townspeople gather in expectation around the animal.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers in Gujarat told how Kumarapala, proud of his teacher, had Hemachandra’s grammar paraded on an elephant, as if it were a king. Tradition remembered a book as a royal treasure.

i18n.hi: बाद के गुजराती कथाकारों ने सुनाया कि कुमारपाल ने अपने गुरु के गौरव में हेमचंद्र की व्याकरण को हाथी पर जुलूस में निकलवाया, जैसे वह खुद राजा हो। परंपरा ने किताब को ही राज-रत्न मान लिया।

panels.shot: close, reverent shot of the massive manuscript resting on the elephant’s platform, with Hemachandra visible in background
panels.action: A large, meticulously bound bundle of palm leaves rests on embroidered cushions atop the elephant’s platform, while in the blurred background Hemachandra stands quietly, hands folded, his eyes lowered.

dialogue.text: Historians treat this elephant procession as court memory, preserved in prabandhas, not a dated entry in an inscription. Yet the image endures because it captures a truth of value: knowledge on a throne.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार इस हाथी-जलूस को अभिलेख की तारीख नहीं, दरबार की स्मृति मानते हैं, जो प्रबंधों में बची। पर यह छवि इसलिए टिक गई कि वह सच्चाई पकड़ती है: ज्ञान को गद्दी पर बिठाया गया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Hemachandra with royal attendants bringing the grammar manuscript into a treasury-like chamber
panels.action: Within a guarded, vaulted chamber, attendants carefully carry the grammar manuscript and set it among jeweled chests and royal insignia, as Hemachandra watches with composed detachment.

dialogue.text: Patan’s memory placed the Siddha-Hema among treasures, not in a dusty corner. When a kingdom decides its grammar belongs with its crown, it is choosing what will outlast its walls.

i18n.hi: पाटण की याद में ‘सिद्धहेम’ को खज़ानों में रखा गया, धूल भरे कोने में नहीं। जब कोई राज्य अपनी व्याकरण को ही मुकुट के साथ रखता है, वह ठहराता है कि दीवारों से ज़्यादा क्या टिकेगा।

panels.shot: soft, contemplative close-up of Hemachandra’s face in old age, light falling on his features
panels.action: In his later years, Hemachandra sits near a window, wrinkles etched gently on his face, eyes distant yet alert as filtered light from the courtyard falls across his features.

dialogue.text: By the mid-1170s, Hemachandra’s court years were drawing to a close. Wars, kings, even Kumarapala’s reign would pass. His chapters, once chanted in Patan, began to travel beyond Gujarat.

i18n.hi: ११७० के आसपास हेमचंद्र के दरबारी वर्ष ढलने लगे। युद्ध, राजा, यहां तक कि कुमारपाल का राज भी गुजर गया। पर पाटण में गाई गई उनकी अध्‍याय-धुनें गुजरात से बाहर तक निकल चलीं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of changing students across generations in the same study hall
panels.action: In the same monastery hall, the scene subtly shifts across time: robes and hairstyles of students change, but each group sits with the same bound manuscript of Hemachandra open before them.

dialogue.text: Paul Dundas and other modern scholars note how his Apabhramsha section became a key witness to the early forms of Gujarati and related tongues, a bridge text that later writers could not ignore.

i18n.hi: पॉल डुंडस और अन्य विद्वान बताते हैं कि उनका अपभ्रम्श हिस्सा शुरुआती गुजराती और उससे जुड़ी बोलियों का अहम साक्षी बन गया — ऐसा सेतु-पाठ जिसे बाद के लेखक अनदेखा न कर सके।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of a map-like ground showing Patan, Dhandhuka, Khambhat, Nagaur and Dhara linked by lines of script
panels.action: On a stylized map underfoot, the names Patan, Dhandhuka, Khambhat, Nagaur and Dhara appear as small cityscapes, linked by flowing lines of script while Hemachandra strides calmly along one of the lines.

dialogue.text: Texts copied in Patan found readers in towns like Dhandhuka and Khambhat, in courts at Nagaur and Dhara. In an age of fractured polities, a Jain monk’s rules gave their languages a shared spine.

i18n.hi: पाटण में नकल हुए ग्रंथ धंधुका और खंभात जैसे नगरों, नागौर और धार जैसे दरबारों में पहुंचे। टूटे-बिखरे राज्यों के दौर में एक जैन मुनि के नियमों ने उनकी भाषाओं को एक रीढ़ दी।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a modern-looking Gujarati manuscript page fading into Hemachandra’s palm-leaf text
panels.action: A neat page of later Gujarati script fades into the older, denser lines of Hemachandra’s palm-leaf manuscript, with his faint silhouette hovering between them like a bridge.

dialogue.text: Hemachandra did not invent Gujarati. But by treating its ancestor as worthy of rule and measure, he helped give later Gujarati writers a framework in which their words could be weighed and remembered.

i18n.hi: हेमचंद्र ने गुजराती नहीं गढ़ी। पर उसके पूर्वज को नियम और माप के काबिल मानकर उन्होंने बाद के गुजराती लेखकों को ऐसा ढांचा दिया, जिसमें उनके शब्द तौले और याद किए जा सकें।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Hemachandra walking away down a colonnade, shelves of manuscripts towering on either side
panels.action: Hemachandra walks slowly down a long stone colonnade lined with towering shelves of manuscripts reaching into shadow, his small figure receding as light filters in from the far end.

dialogue.text: Kings like the Solankis of Gujarat built walls, tanks and towers. Hemachandra built a grammar that could ride an elephant and then outlive the elephant, the palace and the crown that carried it.

i18n.hi: गुजरात के सोलंकी जैसे राजा दीवारें, ताल और मीनारें बनाते रहे। हेमचंद्र ने ऐसी व्याकरण गढ़ी जो पहले हाथी पर चढ़ी, फिर उस हाथी, उस महल और उस मुकुट से भी ज़्यादा देर तक जीवित रही।

title_i18n.hi: हेमचंद्र की व्याकरण हाथी पर सवार

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Jain Monk Made a Kingdom Speak Forever
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहां एक जैन साधु ने भाषा को अमर कर दिया
